thread.title: Amazon (AMZN) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Amazon (AMZN) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo
Can Amazon’s ( AMZN ) earnings be the catalyst that reverse the recent declines among the FAANG stocks? Of course, I’m referring to its peers Facebook ( FB ), Apple ( AAPL ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ).
The e-commerce giant is set to report third quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing Thursday. Like most tech stocks, Amazon shares have been under pressure, falling 8.5% over the past thirty days and almost 4% in three months. And since reaching its all-time high of $2,050.50 on Sept. 4, the stock has corrected as much as 15%. But with the shares still up some 50% year to date, compared with a 3% rise in the S&P 500 index, there’s very little to complain about.
The company has crushed its earnings estimates in the past four quarters. And management last quarter issued Q3 guidance for revenue and earnings to come above Street expectations. Still, while Amazon, which has spoiled investors with breathtaking growth and earnings beats, will most likely do so again, the question remains - will the results get tech stocks out of the lull they have been in?
In the three months that ended September, the Seattle-based company is expected to earn $3.12 per share on revenue of $57.08 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 43 cents per share on revenue of $43.74 billion. For the full year, ending in December, EPS is expected to rise 280% year over year to $17.34 per share, while full year revenue of $234.9 billion would rise 32% year over year.
The company is not only investing massively for growth, but that level of spending tends to impact the bottom line, making earnings — which soared almost 1200% in Q2 — unpredictable. It’s likely that some of the stock’s pullback has weighed on this quarter. In the second quarter, the company’s North America segment, which is its largest source of revenue, was the biggest profit driver, contributing $1.8 billion to Amazon's total profit of $3.0 billion.
Can the torrid growth in North America, which has offset profit losses in international markets, continue? Just as important, North America — for the first time — exceeded the profits of Amazon Web Services (AWS), which has traditionally been the company’s bread-and-butter business. Last quarter, AWS, its cloud computing service, was still solid, delivering profits of $1.6 billion.
Notably, AWS, which has received intense competition from Microsoft ( MSFT ), is showing no signs of slowing down, with revenue rising 49%, compared to 42% in the Q2 of 2017. Just as impressive, Amazon is finding ways to squeeze more profits out of its businesses as evidenced by the gain in operating margin, which came in at 26.9%, up from 22.3% last year. To what extent can these trends continue?
Assuming AWS grows in a range of 45% to 47% this quarter, that translates to total revenue around $6 billion, enough to surpass Street forecast of $5.98 billion. Combined with its array of growth initiatives such as its artificial intelligence-powered virtual assistant business, pharmacy aspirations and Whole Foods, among others, Amazon stock is poised to drive higher. Whether it takes its FAANG peers for the ride? That’s another matter.
